rule: Extend an existing `is_authorized_*` method with an optional parameter rather than adding a parallel `is_authorized_*_for_<entity>` method to the `BaseAuthManager` interface.
trigger: new method added to BaseAuthManager whose name matches `is_authorized_.*_for_` pattern
rationale: A separate method duplicates the whole auth-manager interface for every new entity type; an optional parameter keeps the interface consistent with all existing `is_authorized_*` methods.

rule: Do not set `document.title` dynamically inside React components for Airflow UI pages; the global title is already defined in `index.html`.
trigger: `document.title` assignment inside a `useEffect` hook in a `.tsx` file under the Airflow UI source tree
rationale: Airflow is a self-hosted tool, not a public website; SEO-motivated title overrides are unnecessary and conflict with the global title already provided by `index.html`.

evidence.excerpt: isn't the title already set in the index.html?

rule: Re-use `resolve_user_from_token` (in `core_api/security.py`) instead of calling `get_auth_manager().get_user_from_token` directly in middleware or route code.
rationale: Centralising token-to-user resolution in one helper avoids duplicating error-handling logic and keeps auth middleware consistent.

rule: Name JWT duration parameters `valid_for` (a relative duration), not `expiry` or `expires_at` (which imply an absolute timestamp).
trigger: parameter named `expiry` or `expires_at` on a JWT-generation method that actually receives a TTL integer/timedelta
rationale: The argument is a relative duration fed to `valid_for`, not an absolute expiry timestamp; using `expiry` misleads callers about the expected value.

evidence.excerpt: should probably call this argument `valid_for` since that is what it is being used for

rule: When cursor pagination encounters an unparseable cursor token (e.g. malformed UUID for a `Uuid` column), raise HTTP 400 rather than silently falling back to the original value.
trigger: `except (ValueError, Exception):` block inside `_coerce_value` or cursor-parsing code that returns the raw `value` instead of raising
rationale: Silent fallback accepts the cursor but produces incorrect or empty results; an HTTP 400 communicates clearly that the token is invalid.

evidence.excerpt: treat UUID parse failure as an invalid cursor token and raise HTTP 400

rule: Keyset cursor pagination over nullable sort columns must use null-aware comparisons (e.g. `IS NULL` tie-break or `COALESCE`) matching the ORDER BY null-ordering semantics; bare `col > NULL` comparisons silently break paging.
trigger: cursor `or_clauses.append(and_(*eq_conditions, col > value))` where `col` can be nullable without a corresponding `IS NULL` guard
rationale: SQL comparisons against NULL evaluate to NULL/false, causing keyset-paginated queries over nullable sort keys to return empty or inconsistent result sets.

evidence.excerpt: breaks when any cursor value is None, causing paging to return empty

rule: Use `if/elif` (not sequential `if`) when filter parameter branches for mutually exclusive bound conditions (`lower_bound` vs `lower_bound_excluded`) to avoid emitting redundant SQL WHERE clauses.
trigger: two consecutive `if self.value and self.value.lower_bound` / `if self.value and self.value.lower_bound_excluded` blocks that should be mutually exclusive
rationale: Sequential `if` statements emit two independent WHERE predicates to the DB; the second shadows the first at query time but adds unnecessary SQL complexity.

evidence.excerpt: should be an if/else … no need to make the emitted sql query more complex

rule: Use `SerializedDAG` (imported under `TYPE_CHECKING` from `airflow.serialization.serialized_objects`) as the concrete type annotation for DAG-bearing attributes in API parameter/datamodel classes rather than `Any`.
trigger: property or attribute typed `None | Any` in a parameter/datamodel class where the value is a serialized DAG object
rationale: Using `Any` discards type information; `SerializedDAG` is the correct concrete type and is safely importable under `TYPE_CHECKING` to avoid circular imports.

rule: Queries that use `_RegexParam` must be wrapped with `apply_regex_query_timeout`; document this obligation in the `_RegexParam` docstring.
trigger: use of `_RegexParam` or `regex_param_factory` in a route without a corresponding `apply_regex_query_timeout` call, or a `_RegexParam` class/factory lacking a docstring warning about the timeout requirement
rationale: Regex matching against large tables without a timeout can cause unbounded server-side CPU consumption; `paginated_select` should guard against this, and callsites outside that helper are also at risk.

evidence.excerpt: caller query using this should time bound calling `apply_regex_query_timeout`

rule: In `SortParam.get_resolved_columns()`, derive `attr_name` after applying `to_replace` so that the resolved name matches the actual ORM attribute used in ORDER BY and cursor encoding.
trigger: `attr_name = lstriped_orderby` set before the `to_replace` mapping is applied in `SortParam`
rationale: Setting `attr_name` before `to_replace` causes cursor tokens to encode `null` for sort fields that map to a different ORM attribute name, silently breaking keyset pagination.

evidence.excerpt: attr_name is set before applying to_replace … cursor tokens will encode null

rule: When silently coercing an unrecognised stored value to `None` in a Pydantic validator (e.g. for `asset_expression`), emit a `log.warning` so that schema drift between the server and the DB remains observable.
trigger: `except ValidationError: return None` in a Pydantic validator without a preceding `log.warning` call when `value` is not `None`
rationale: Silent coercion cannot distinguish a genuinely legacy row from a new shape the model does not yet cover; a warning keeps drift observable while still degrading gracefully.

evidence.excerpt: log a warning when a non-None value is coerced away, so drift stays observable

rule: Boolean timetable properties used by the API (e.g. `is_backfillable`) must be persisted in `DagModel` via a DB migration rather than derived at runtime from `timetable_summary` string matching.
trigger: a `frozenset` of timetable summary strings used in a datamodel or route to derive a boolean DAG property instead of reading a `DagModel` column
rationale: Hard-coded string sets diverge from the `.periodic` / `timetable_partitioned` attributes already stored on `DagModel`; a DB column stays consistent across serialization and avoids string-matching drift.

evidence.excerpt: Is it possible to store that in the DagModel via a migration?

rule: When redacting a dict value (e.g. Trigger kwargs) in an API response serializer, keep it as a JSON-serialisable dict rather than wrapping it in `str()`.
trigger: `str(redact(value))` where `value` is a dict in a Pydantic response serializer or validator
rationale: Applying `str()` to a dict produces Python's repr string instead of valid JSON, breaking API consumers that expect a structured object.

evidence.excerpt: value is almost certainly a dict … relying on stringification of a python dict

rule: Compare `DagRunType` enum members directly (e.g. `DagRunType.MANUAL`) rather than their `.value` attribute when checking membership in `dm.allowed_run_types`.
trigger: `DagRunType.<member>.value not in dm.allowed_run_types` (accessing `.value` before membership test)
rationale: Airflow stores `DagRunType` enum members (not raw strings) in `allowed_run_types`; comparing via `.value` introduces an inconsistent access pattern and may silently fail if the field is typed.

evidence.excerpt: accessing enum value through .value is not consistent

rule: When multiple code paths implement partition-date-window localization with different interval conventions (inclusive vs half-open), add a cross-reference comment or consolidate to avoid silent drift.
trigger: inline `timetable.localize_partition_datetime` call in a route that duplicates the logic in `DagRun.apply_partition_date_window` with a different interval boundary
rationale: Two localization conventions for partition date windows is a drift risk; a future reader may assume they match and introduce subtle off-by-one errors.

evidence.excerpt: two partition-date localization conventions is a drift risk

rule: Validate that a requested `try_number` actually exists in the DB before using it to generate extra links; return 404 for non-existent try numbers.
trigger: `ti.try_number = try_number` assignment in an extra-links route without a preceding DB check that the try number exists
rationale: Without validation, callers can request links for try numbers that never existed, which should produce a 404 rather than silently generating links for phantom attempts.

evidence.excerpt: no validation … you can get link generation for tries that do not exist

rule: Do not use the name `task_instance` for a variable that may hold either a `TaskInstance` or a `TaskInstanceHistory`; use a neutral name (`row`, `entity`, `model`) to avoid type confusion.
trigger: variable named `task_instance` assigned from a query that can return either `TI` or `TIH` ORM objects
rationale: `TaskInstance` and `TaskInstanceHistory` are different models with different interfaces; a shared name implies the caller can always treat the result as a TI, which is incorrect.

evidence.excerpt: those are not the same model and don't expose the same interface

rule: Place `_ImportPathCallbackDef` (and similar callback-definition objects) in the domain model module (e.g. `models/test_connection.py`) rather than directly in the route handler file.
trigger: `_ImportPathCallbackDef` or `ExecutorCallback` construction inlined inside a route handler function body
rationale: Route files should not own domain model objects; moving the definition to the relevant model module improves reuse and keeps route handlers thin.

rule: Use `entity.name` (not `entity.pool` or other wrong attribute) when collecting pool names in bulk-action validation; verify attribute names against the actual Pydantic body class before building error lists.
trigger: `invalid_entities.append(entity.pool)` or similarly wrong attribute access on a `PoolBody` instance inside bulk-action validation
rationale: `PoolBody` exposes `name`, not `pool`; using the wrong attribute raises `AttributeError` (500) instead of the intended HTTP 400 response.

evidence.excerpt: entity.pool will likely raise AttributeError (500) instead of returning 400
